recheck.step2_semantic_argument: CONFIRMED SOUND — the fix is `source.get(after_q..end) == Some(name)`. after_q = i+1 where bytes[i]==b'?' A non-char-boundary end's slice would include ≥1 byte >=0x80 (UTF-8 continuation), which can NEVER equal an all-ASCII hole name (all bytes <0x80) — so refusing the match is not merely panic-safe, it is CORRECT: no real match is skipped. Fall-through to the verbatim per-char copy is the right behavior. Slice audit CONFIRMED: the only other slices are the fallback `source[i..].chars().next()` and `source[i..i+ch_len]`; `i` is a char boundary by induction (base i=0; matched branch sets i=end which get() proved is a boundary; fallback branch advances by the char's own len_utf8) — so both are boundary-safe. bytes[i]/bytes.get(end) are byte-indexed (no boundary concern). No residual slice can panic.

critical_bugs.title: F1 boundary-safe scan panics on valid UTF-8 (char-boundary slice) — a REGRESSION from the old code, reachable from production surfaces, and a direct violation of the spec's explicit char-boundary-safety requirement
critical_bugs.evidence_code: if end <= bytes.len() && &source[after_q..end] == name {   // end<=len guards OOB but NOT char-boundary; end = after_q + name.len() can land INSIDE a multibyte char
critical_bugs.root_cause: At each `?`, the scan computes end = (i+1) + name.len() and slices &source[after_q..end] to compare against a candidate hole name. `end <= bytes.len()` is checked but `source.is_char_boundary(end)` is NOT. When a hole-name candidate's length reaches into a following multibyte UTF-8 character, `end` is not on a char boundary and the str slice panics ('byte index N is not a char boundary'). The comparison never even executes — the panic is in the slice itself.
critical_bugs.reproduction_standalone: Extracted the exact function into a standalone binary. Input source `// tuned ?W\u{20AC} tile` (i.e. `?W` immediately followed by the 3-byte '€') with assignments {WG:128}: candidate 'WG' (len 2) makes end land at byte 12, inside '€' (bytes 11..14) -> panic 'byte index 12 is not a char boundary'.
critical_bugs.reproduction_real_cli: Built ./target/debug/axc. File with a comment line `// tuned ?W\xe2\x82\xac budget` + one kernel using ?WG. `axc compile panic.axc -o panic.spv --strategy-value WG=64` -> process aborts with exit code 101 (Rust panic), no DriverError, no clean diagnostic.
critical_bugs.regression_proof: The OLD Pass-1 code (`result.replace("?WG", "128")`) was run on the identical input and returned the string UNTOUCHED with no panic. So F1 — whose stated purpose is a 'SOUND, not a bandaid' robustness rewrite — introduced a crash on input that previously compiled fine.
critical_bugs.reachability: substitute_strategy_holes is `pub` and called by compile_source_with_assignments{,_kernel} -> `axc compile --strategy-value`, `axc compile --all --strategy-value` (main.rs run_compile), the autotuner bench path, `axc rewrite-verify`, and MCP compile_variant / bench_variant. All feed user-controlled .axc source. A `?`+partial-name+multibyte-char sequence anywhere in the source (including a `//` comment, since substitution runs before the lexer) triggers it.
critical_bugs.spec_violation: The pessimistic design-review mandate and §4/§8 explicitly required the byte-scan to 'index bytes safely, no char-boundary panic on slicing.' This is exactly the missed guarantee.
critical_bugs.fix: One line: change the guard to `if end <= bytes.len() && source.is_char_boundary(end) && &source[after_q..end] == name`, OR replace the slice+compare with `if source.get(after_q..end) == Some(name)` (Option-returning, panic-free). A non-char-boundary end can never equal an ASCII hole name, so refusing to match there is trivially correct (it falls through to copying the char verbatim). Add an AT with a `?`+multibyte-char fixture.
critical_bugs.routing: Coder (implementation defect; the design already mandated char-boundary safety — not a design change).

warnings.title: `--all` multi-file emit is not write-atomic — a mid-loop I/O failure leaves orphan artifacts
warnings.line: run_compile --all loop (writes <stem>.<k>.spv then its sidecar, per kernel, in sequence)
warnings.assessment: The compile-failure orphan case IS correctly closed: `compile_module_all` compiles (and thus cross-validates) EVERY kernel BEFORE any file is written, so a sibling-compile failure writes zero files (matches spec §13). The residual is pure file-I/O: if kernel[0].spv writes, then its sidecar or kernel[1].spv fails (disk full / permission / ENOSPC), the already-written files remain — no tempfile-rename or cleanup discipline. This is IDENTICAL to the pre-existing single-kernel compile_file behavior (.spv then sidecar; a sidecar failure orphans the .spv) and spec §13 only guarantees no-partial-output for the ambiguous/compile-failure case, not for I/O failures between writes. CLASSIFIED AS ACCEPTED RESIDUAL, not a defect — noted for honesty, does not block.

summary: M3.21's N-separate-modules architecture is sound and the milestone clears every adversarial probe I ran EXCEPT one: metadata pairing verified with a 3-kernel distinct-dims fixture (each sidecar+spv pairs its own kernel), select_kernel is a single shared fail-closed helper across CLI+MCP+autotuner, strip_all handles 3 blocks, the at_2835 equality clause is unweakened, spirv-val runs in-process clean on both example kernels, union_module_holes' prefix/conflict guards are non-vacuous and provably sound, fail-closed CLI writes no partial output, and the QA MEDIUM --size gap was already fixed correctly. The blocking issue is PCR-1: the F1 boundary-safe substitution scan — the milestone's flagship robustness fix — slices `&source[after_q..end]` without a char-boundary check, so a hole-name candidate whose length reaches into a following multibyte UTF-8 char panics the process. I reproduced this both in an extracted standalone and through the real `axc compile --strategy-value WG=64` CLI (exit 101), and proved it is a REGRESSION (the old str::replace returned the same input untouched). It is reachable from compile/--all/rewrite-verify/autotuner/MCP on any user source containing `?`+partial-name+multibyte-char (even inside a comment, since substitution precedes lexing), and it directly violates the design mandate's explicit 'no char-boundary panic on slicing' requirement. The fix is ~1 line (`source.is_char_boundary(end)` guard or `source.get(after_q..end)`), plus an AT with a multibyte fixture. Verdict NEEDS_REVISION: route PCR-1 to the Coder; PCR-2 is an accepted residual and PCR-3 is already resolved — neither blocks.
